title: End-to-End Evidence & Containment Playbook for Cross-Region Inference Incidents
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the operational steps, evidence requirements, and containment actions for inference-related security incidents that span multiple geographic regions or data jurisdictions ("cross-region inference incidents"). It maps RBAC/auth checks, audit logging retrieval, data residency considerations, secure SDLC artifacts, and compliance evidence packaging into a single end-to-end procedure.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Enable fast, defensible incident response and compliance evidence assembly when model-serving or inference requests trigger security concerns across region boundaries.
- Scope: Applies to incidents involving Redwood-hosted inference endpoints, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC) deployments where requests, data, or logs cross jurisdictional boundaries.
- Not in scope: Customer-managed on-prem systems not connected to Redwood telemetry collection (see owner_team escalation).

Stakeholders and ownership:
| Role | Team | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Incident Commander (IC) | eng-sre / security (rotating) | Triage ownership, external comms, regulatory notification decisioning |
| Evidence Custodian | security | Assemble packaged evidence, sign-off for retention & export |
| Runtime Lead | eng-serving-runtime | Collect runtime traces, model variant mappings, KV-cache snapshots |
| Audit Logging Lead | eng-infra | Retrieve immutable audit streams and sign timestamps |
| Legal & Compliance | finance-legal | Regulatory notification, data residency approvals, privileged exception review |
| Customer Success | customer-success | Customer comms (if customer visible) and contractual obligations |

Incident severity classification (quick reference):
1) Sev1: Active exfiltration or unauthorized cross-border data access confirmed. Immediate regulator/DAO notification potential.
2) Sev2: Unauthorized inference outputs (PII leakage) suspected but scope unknown.
3) Sev3: Non-customer-impacting auth misconfiguration discovered in routing/policy.

Triage checklist (first 30 minutes):
1. IC announces incident channel (secure Slack + incident document).
2. Snapshot RBAC state: export relevant policy bindings via internal tool (command example below).
   - Command: redwood-auth export-bindings --scope "<tenant|org|service>" --output /tmp/bindings-$(date +%s).json
3. Lock down privileged paths: perform just-in-time disable on implicated service accounts.
   - Command: iamctl disable --service-account <id> --reason "incident-<id>"
4. Preserve raw audit stream: ask Audit Logging Lead to seal and snapshot the region-specific Kafka topic and immutable object store.

Evidence collection matrix (required for regulatory and audit packages):
- RBAC & Auth artifacts:
  - Current and historical role bindings (exported JSON) for the affected tenant/org/service (retain 2x incident window).
  - Access tokens and token-issuance logs (issue/refresh/rotation events) from authn service.
  - Privilege elevation events (JITA activations) with who/when/for-what.
- Audit logging artifacts:
  - Immutable audit blob range covering T0 - T+48h (UTC). Include structured events (request_id, principal_id, route, model_version, response_size, geoip).
  - Raw transport logs (ingress/egress, LB traces) and service-level traces (span traces) correlated by request_id.
- Data residency and storage artifacts:
  - Storage bucket/object manifests showing residency region tags and object creation timestamps.
  - KMS envelope logs showing key usage and region-bound KMS operations.
- Secure SDLC artifacts (if suspected code/packaging issue):
  - Signed build manifest, container digest, image provenance (SBOM), and CI/CD pipeline run ids for the deployed model-serving revision.
- Incident-specific snapshots:
  - KV cache head snapshots (if model cache reuse may have caused data bleed).
  - Batcher policy state and active batching windows.

Evidence packaging standard (what to deliver to regulators/auditors):
1. Evidence manifest (JSON list) with SHA256 checksums for each artifact and canonical timestamps.
2. Readme describing provenance and chain-of-custody for each artifact.
3. Redacted sample of affected inference requests (PII redaction applied at source) plus algorithm used for redaction.
4. Signed attestation from Evidence Custodian.

Retention and export rules (table):
| Artifact type | Minimum retention (internal) | Export allowed? | Storage location | Export notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Audit event blobs | 7 years | Yes (case-by-case, legal sign-off) | immutable-archive/region/{r} | Exports must include signature and manifest |
| RBAC bindings snapshot | 3 years | Yes (redacted) | auth-evidence-store | Must include admin approval |
| Token issuance logs | 1 year | No (sensitive) | secure-log-vault | Export prohibited without court order |
| Build manifests/SBOM | 5 years | Yes | sdlc-provenance-store | Include CI job ids and commit SHAs |
| KV-cache snapshots | 90 days | No (contains potential customer data) | ephemeral-forensics | Only accessible to security + legal w/ approval |

Key operational commands and examples (for responders):
- Export recent audit events for request_id X from ES cluster:
  curl -s -u readonly:$(cat /etc/audit/es-readonly-token) "https://es.internal/_search?q=request_id:REQUEST_ID&size=10000" > /tmp/audit-REQUEST_ID.ndjson

- Seal and snapshot Kafka topic (audit-topic-REGION-A) to immutable store:
  kafka-dump --topic audit-topic-REGION-A --from-offset <start> --to-offset <end> --out /tmp/audit-REGION-A-$(date +%s).ndjson
  objectstore put --bucket immutable-archive-region-a /tmp/audit-REGION-A-$(date +%s).ndjson --tag sealed-by=incident-<id>

- Example auth export (RBAC):
  redwood-auth export-bindings --scope tenant:acme-corp --since 2024-11-10T00:00:00Z --output /tmp/acme-bindings.json

Containment and fallback policy (decision matrix):
- If evidence shows active cross-border data flow with unauthorized principal: immediate partial shutdown of cross-region routing for affected model and region-level failover to region-local variant.
- If only misconfiguration with no confirmed data leakage: apply corrective policy patch (policy id) and schedule a canary verification before re-enabling routing.
- Always prefer region-local fallback when available; document the reason and timestamp.

Forensic integrity and cryptographic stamping:
- All artifacts moved to the evidence store must be hashed with SHA256 and timestamped with the internal timestamping service (ts.sign). The Evidence Custodian adds a signed manifest:

  # Example manifest entry (line format)
  sha256:af3b... | audit-REGION-A-1672531200.ndjson | sealed-by:incident-2024-123 | ts:2024-11-15T13:04:00Z

Regulatory notification thresholds and timelines:
- Confidential data confirmed exfiltrated outside authorized jurisdictions: notify Legal within 2 hours and regulators (per region) within 72 hours if required by local law.
- PII exposure limited to <10 users (customer visible): IC to consult Legal; consider deferred notification pending scope confirmation but no later than 48 hours.

Exception handling and risk acceptance:
1. If evidence cannot be exported due to data residency policies, Legal must issue an exception request by completing the Exception Request Template and escalate to the cross-functional board within 24 hours.
2. Exception approval requires at minimum: security sign-off, runtime lead mitigation plan, and compliance/legal sign-off (emails archived).
3. All approved exceptions must be logged into the Authorization Exception Register (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/exception-register).

Post-incident activities (72-hour and 30-day):
- 72-hour: Evidence package finalized and handed to Legal; regulatory notification goes out if required. Conduct an initial root-cause hypothesis and short blameless rundown.
- 30-day: Formal Post-Incident Review (PIR) with engineering, security, legal and customer-success. Deliverables: RCA, remediation backlog, policy changes, test-case additions to eval harness, and a compliance evidence audit confirming retention rules were followed.

SDLC and prevention controls (recommended):
- Enforce signed image and SBOM verification at deploy time for the runtime and model-serving artifacts.
- Require staged regional config tests that assert no cross-region data flows in canary mode.
- Add unit/regression tests that assert policy bindings for routing and tenant isolation.

Templates and attachments (appendix):
- Evidence manifest template (JSON sample).
- Exception request template (DOC).
- Sample redaction script (Python) used when preparing PII-sanitized samples.

Appendix A — Quick reference scrubbing example (Python pseudocode):
  def redact_user_text(payload):
      # naive example - run through production redactor with policy id
      return re.sub(r"\b\d{9,}\b", "[REDACTED]", payload)

Appendix B — Contact list (oncall rotation):
1. Security oncall: +1-555-0101 (Slack: #security-oncall)
2. Eng SRE oncall: +1-555-0102
3. Legal urgent: legal-urgent@redwood.ai
